Marcus, thanks for the call earlier. As part of our security review and the on-prem/VPC deployment plan, our infrastructure team needs explicit carveouts in the SLA for any incidents that are caused by our customer-managed networking (transit gateways, on-prem firewall policies, MPLS links to the VPC).

Attached is the list of exception types we need (loss of transit, BGP flaps, packet loss > 0.5% on the customer egress, and planned maintenance windows at our colo). We also want to understand whether there are any mitigation playbooks Redwood can commit to (for example, cross-region failover, additional retries, or a degraded-mode API) so we can show our security/compliance folks how failures will be handled.

On Fri, 21 Sep 2028 at 11:27 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:

Marcus / Daniel — I reviewed the list. From a runtime and serving perspective, the relevant boundaries are:

1) Control plane vs data plane: Redwood controls our inference runtime and KV cache; however, when customer routing prevents forwarding (BGP blackholes, MPLS outages, transit egress packet loss), token delivery and latency cannot be guaranteed.
2) KV cache & continuous batching: if network instability causes repeated TCP resets to our customer VPC endpoints, we can fall back to a lower-throughput path but that will increase tail latency and reduce effective throughput.

Suggested draft clause (high level):
"Customer Network Exceptions: Redwood Inference's uptime and latency commitments do not apply to incidents where the root cause is within Customer-controlled network infrastructure, including but not limited to customer-managed transit gateways, on-premises WAN links, customer-configured routing/policy, or third-party network carriers contracted by Customer. In such events Redwood will provide best-effort mitigation, including recommended configuration changes, fallback routing where available, and operational runbooks, but will not be liable for uptime credits tied to the affected endpoints."

Specific asks from us to make the exception operationally manageable:
- A network diagram showing ingress/egress points and transit carriers.
- Point-of-contact and scheduled maintenance windows for the colo carrier.
- Agree to a joint post-incident RCA for any major outage that triggers our incident review process.

I attached a short plain-text draft that Monica/legal can massage. Happy to iterate on the trigger language — e.g., require a carrier-provided incident report as root-cause evidence if necessary.
